references.text: God promises to send his angel ahead of the people of Israel to lead them on their way—an early background for the motif of a messenger who goes before and prepares the way.
Direct source of the quotation in Luke 7:27. Malachi prophesies: "Se, jeg sender min budbærer, han skal rydde veien foran meg." Jesus applies this to John the Baptist.
Isaiah prophesies about a voice crying out in the wilderness: "Rydd Herrens vei, jevn en hovedvei i ørkenen for vår Gud." This was early linked to John the Baptist's role as the forerunner.
The parallel passage in Matthew where Jesus quotes exactly the same scripture from Malachi concerning John the Baptist as the sent messenger.
Mark opens his gospel by quoting the same Malachi passage and applies it to John the Baptist as the one who prepares the way for Jesus.
John the Baptist identifies himself with Isaiah's prophecy about the voice crying out in the wilderness, which aligns with his role as the way-preparer.
Zechariah prophesies about his son John that he shall "gå foran Herren og rydde hans veier"—a direct reference to the forerunner role confirmed in Luke 7:27.

The immediate context where Jesus asks the crowd what they went out into the wilderness to see, and declares that John is more than a prophet—something he then supports with the quotation in verse 27.
